lessons.lesson: The gimlat siud income test shipped for three versions with no NIS figure anywhere in the skill, so the test could not be executed at all. The official test is four filing-month tables x three bands x three family statuses. Reproduce multi-row rate tables in full; a qualitative description of a numeric test is not a rate table.

The couple band was wrong in the user's disfavour: couples get the FULL benefit up to 1.5x the individual threshold and the reduced rate up to 2.25x, not one shared household ceiling. When a rule has a couple variant, read the couple row rather than generalising from the individual row.

btl.gov.il/benefits/Long_Term_Care/benefit_level/Pages/default.aspx renders levels 1-6 client-side and the string for hours never appears in the served HTML. The per-level pages level1.aspx through level6.aspx ARE server-rendered and readable with plain curl. When a hub page is JS-rendered, look for per-item pages before reaching for a browser.

Percent-encoded Hebrew kolzchut URLs in the skill body generated 14 phantom percentage claims in the evidence gate (%D7 read as a percentage). Keep literal Hebrew URLs in the body; keep encoded forms in evidence.json, which the gate skips.

The evidence gate matches per locale: a Hebrew claim of an amount followed by shekel does not match a raw_snippet that writes the same number followed by NIS. Write the claim field in English with NIS and the raw_snippet in the source's Hebrew, so both forms are present across the entry.

An earlier draft of this review asserted that 26 hours is the base at level 6 and 30 is base plus the Israeli-caregiver supplement, taken from a secondary source's historical framing. The official BTL level pages present 30 as the headline and 26 as the foreign-worker variant, which is how the skill already had it. Read the primary source before inverting a table's semantics.

lessons: CORRECTION to the v1.4.0 commit message: it states the hours-table columns were inverted and fixed. They were not. Phase 3 raised the inversion from Kol-Zchut's historical framing; the official BTL per-level pages present 30 as the headline and 26 as the foreign-worker variant, which is how the skill already had it. The table orientation was NOT changed. What WAS added to that table: the 50%-reduced row, the level 1 election, day-centre conversion, and the cash-conversion cap column. Levels 1-6 are now each read from a server-rendered levelN.aspx text layer with its own evidence entry, so nothing is inferred.

deferred.item: Attendance allowance (kitzvat shirutim meyuchadim) has zero mentions in the skill. It carries a hard deadline: someone who became dependent before retirement age must claim within 6 months of retirement age or lose the entitlement permanently. 2026 rates: 50% 1,943 NIS, 112% 4,501, 188% 7,181, 235% 9,126, ventilator supplement 10,774, two-caregiver supplement 7,182. Not counted as income in the siud means test. Source: kolzchut.org.il/he/kitzvat shirutim meyuchadim, official btl.gov.il/benefits/Attendance_Allowance.

deferred.item: Supported decision-making (tomech hachlatot), the third and less restrictive status between an enduring POA and guardianship, from the 2016 amendment to the Legal Capacity and Guardianship Law. Also the expression-of-wishes document. Step 6 currently presents a binary, which pushes families with mild-dementia parents toward disproportionate guardianship.

The description's routing note excludes 'general Bituach Leumi benefits'. That exclusion is what let the attendance allowance and the hospitalisation rules fall through: they are elder-care mechanics, not general BL topics. Narrow the note when the deferred items land.
